tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear Path for Target Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk that is not on top, relocate every smaller disk that sits above it to other pegs so the target becomes the topmost disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that has smaller disks above it on its current peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If disk 4 is under disk 1 on peg 0, first move disk 1 elsewhere, then move disk 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Build Goal Stack in Decreasing Size
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Construct the final tower on the goal peg by placing disks from the largest down to the smallest, ensuring each larger disk is already in place before a smaller one is added.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When assembling the final configuration on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 5 to peg 2, next place disk 4 on top, then disk 3, then disk 2, then disk 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Phase Planning (Move‑k‑Disks)
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to an auxiliary peg, move the k‑th (largest) disk to its destination, then move the k‑1 disks onto it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a group of disks between pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move three disks from peg A to peg B: move the top two to peg C, move the third to B, then move the two from C to B.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never move a small disk onto the goal peg before all larger disks that must sit below it have already been placed there.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving any small disk to the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not place disk 1 on the goal peg until disks 5, 4, 3, 2 are already stacked.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Legal Move Invariant
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A move is legal only if the source disk is the topmost on its peg and the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 onto a peg whose top is disk 2 is illegal because 3 > 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat Existing Goal Disks as Fixed Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Once a disk is correctly placed on the goal peg with all larger disks beneath it also correctly placed, treat this stack as immutable and never move those disks again.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After a disk has reached its final position on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After placing disk 5 at the bottom of the goal peg, never move disk 5 again.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Exploit the Smallest Disk’s Flexibility
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints, making it an ideal temporary buffer for clearing paths.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a temporary placeholder to free larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 1 to an empty peg to allow moving disk 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Post‑Construction Verification
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full move list, replay the moves from the initial configuration to confirm that each move is legal and the final configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have produced a candidate move sequence, before final submission.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Simulate the moves step‑by‑step and compare the final state to the target configuration.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Generate Moves Recursively with Explicit Disk IDs
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When implementing the recursive Hanoi algorithm, explicitly name the disk being moved in each step to avoid ambiguity and ensure correct move encoding.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: While constructing the move list, either manually or programmatically.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Record a move as [3, 0, 2] meaning “move disk 3 from peg 0 to peg 2”.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move Two Smallest Disks as a Unit
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a target disk is blocked by exactly two smaller disks, clear the path using a three‑move pattern: move the smallest to an auxiliary peg, move the second smallest to the target peg, then move the smallest onto the second smallest.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the top two disks on a peg are the smallest ones and you need to free the third disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: With disks 1 and 2 atop disk 4, move 1 to peg B, move 2 to peg C (target), then move 1 onto 2.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may focus on moving a particular disk identifier without checking the size relationship, forgetting the rule that larger disks cannot be placed on smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before adding a move, verify that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may select a disk based on its number rather than its position, overlooking the top‑only rule.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the chosen disk is the topmost disk on its source peg before issuing the move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: The sequence of moves ends with a configuration that differs from the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop early, lose track of the required final ordering, or mis‑order moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After generating the move list, simulate the entire sequence and compare the final state to the goal; if they differ, continue planning.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Using the wrong peg numbers (e.g., 1 instead of 0) when listing moves.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Off‑by‑one errors or confusion about the zero‑based indexing required by the verifier.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Consistently use 0‑based peg indices and double‑check each move’s from and to values.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a small disk onto the goal peg before all larger required disks have been positioned beneath it.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may prioritize moving the smallest disk because it is always legal, ignoring the required ordering on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Follow the “Build Goal Stack in Decreasing Size” principle and only place a small disk on the goal after all larger disks that belong below it are already there.
